Definition: to flee for protection; figuratively, to confide in
BiblicalUsage: Chacah means to flee for protection, to trust, to take refuge. Moses asks where the gods are, the rock in whom they trusted; the bramble invites the trees to trust in its shadow; Boaz tells Ruth a full reward will be given her, because she came to trust under the wings of the God of Israel; and David sings that God is his rock, his shield, his high tower, and his refuge.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe trust is not a feeling but a place — under wings, behind a shield, inside a tower. The bramble offers a shadow and gives thorns; God offers His wings and gives shelter.
